items.title: Culham Trail Access Point Reopens as Eglinton Avenue Sewer Upgrade Wraps Up
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Region has finished upgrading the sanitary sewer and maintenance holes along a stretch of Eglinton Avenue West near Mississauga Road. According to the outlet, region officials said all construction work between Hewicks Lane and The Chase is now complete. The outlet reports the project upgraded sewers that carry wastewater from sinks, tubs, showers and toilets, a task officials said was needed to keep providing high-quality wastewater service. According to insauga.com, traffic on Eglinton Avenue West is expected to return to normal now that the work is done. The outlet reports the completed project also means the Eglinton Avenue West and Barbertown Road access point to the Culham Trail, closed to the public since earlier this year, will reopen.

items.title: Four High-Profile Candidates Pushed Mississauga Turnout Past 2022 Levels, Insauga Reports
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga's bitterly contested mayoral race drew considerably more eligible voters to the polls than the city saw in the 2022 municipal election. According to the outlet, the matchup between incumbent Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie was widened further by one-term councillor and now mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo, who had already challenged Parrish once before in the 2024 byelection to succeed Crombie. The outlet reports Ward 7 councillor Dipika Damerla, who finished a distant fourth and is leaving council as a result, rounded out the four high-profile names that helped drive turnout. According to insauga.com, 191,166 voters cast ballots this time to elect the mayor, 11 city councillors and a slate of school board trustees. The outlet notes that despite the stronger showing, Mississauga's turnout has historically ranked among the lowest in Ontario.

items.title: Peel Police Suspend Toronto Man's Licence After Street Race Near Meadowvale Boulevard
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Regional Police have laid multiple charges against a Toronto man after a street-racing investigation in northwest Mississauga. According to the outlet, officers with the force's Safer Roads Team spotted a vehicle racing with other cars near Meadowpine Boulevard and Meadowvale Boulevard in the early morning hours of Oct. 15. Police said the vehicle was travelling at a high speed in close proximity to pedestrians, creating a significant risk to public safety. The outlet reports investigators identified a suspect and arrested 21-year-old Anthony Fuellos Knox of Toronto that same day. According to insauga.com, Knox was released on an undertaking to appear in Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton, while Safer Roads Team officers seized his vehicle and suspended his driver's licence for 30 days.

items.title: High School Teacher Says He Saw Mayor-elect Coming When Tedjo Was Still a Student
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Alvin Tedjo's former high school teacher said he always expected his student would one day become mayor. According to the newspaper, Tony Oseivhi, who taught communications technology, made the comment after attending Tedjo's first press conference as mayor-elect, held in Celebration Square just minutes from Father Michael Goetz Secondary School. The Star reports Oseivhi joked that Tedjo was already a politician back in high school. According to the outlet, Oseivhi said his former student has always been a skilled communicator. The Star reports Oseivhi said he was "so excited" about his former student's victory.

items.title: Mother Says Emergency Services Were Never Called After Son's Scissor Injury at Mississauga Daycare
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a Mississauga mother is seeking answers after her four-year-old son was injured with scissors at a daycare program. According to the outlet, Nazli Yilmaz said her son suffered a deep wound near his eye requiring stitches after another child struck him during a PLASP after-school program at Cooksville Creek Public School on Oct. 5. The outlet reports Yilmaz said staff cleaned her son up and changed his bloodied clothing but never called emergency medical services before she arrived. According to insauga.com, Yilmaz does not blame the other child, who she says is non-verbal and has special needs, but instead faults the adults supervising the program. The outlet reports she still wants to know why paramedics weren't contacted and how a child was able to access scissors in the first place.

items.title: Tedjo Says His Own Family Hadn't Reached the Victory Party When Networks Called Mississauga's Race
items.summary: CTV News reports Mississauga's mayor-elect, Alvin Tedjo, says even his own family was still on the way to his victory party when the race was called Monday night. According to the outlet, Tedjo told CP24 Breakfast the call came less than 30 minutes after polls closed, catching him off guard while his team still had hundreds of volunteers out in the field. The outlet reports Tedjo defeated incumbent Carolyn Parrish by 22,626 votes and former mayor Bonnie Crombie by 31,288 votes. According to CTV News, Tedjo said people wanted something new and fresh, with new ideas and new energy, after the results came in. The outlet reports nearly 40 per cent of eligible Mississauga residents voted this time, almost double the 21 per cent turnout recorded in 2022.

items.title: Ontario's Police Watchdog Clears OPP Officer After Man Fractures Ribs Fleeing Cannabis Search on Highway 407
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has closed its probe into a Highway 407 traffic stop after determining a man's fractured ribs were not caused by police. According to the outlet, an OPP officer pulled over a westbound vehicle near Mavis Road on the morning of Oct. 11 for a Highway Traffic Act violation and then found an unsealed bag of suspected cannabis on the front console. The SIU says that while the officer searched the trunk, a 36-year-old passenger climbed over the highway guardrail and ran down an embankment, where he tripped and fell. The agency reports the man was taken to the detachment, where he complained of chest pain and difficulty breathing. According to SIU Deputy Director Stacey O'Brien, a review of video footage confirmed no force was used by police beyond handcuffing him during the arrest, and the man's injuries resulted from his own fall while trying to flee.
